title: "Tutorial 9 — Self-check answers"
sidebar: mfml
---

1. Likelihood is exp-quadratic in $\mu$; times a Gaussian prior stays exp-quadratic $\Rightarrow$ Gaussian posterior.  
2. $\mu_n=\sigma_n^2(\mu_0/\sigma_0^2 + n\bar x/\sigma^2)$ with $\sigma_n^{-2}=\sigma_0^{-2}+n\sigma^{-2}$.  
3. $\mu_{\mathrm{MAP}}=\mu_n$ (Gaussian mode = mean).  
4. $\mu_{\mathrm{MAP}}\to\mu_{\mathrm{ML}}=\bar x$.  
5. $\sigma^2$: known noise of observations; $\sigma_0^2$: prior uncertainty about the mean $\mu$.
